analysis: Partial correlation of pollution vs income controlling for population density
density_source: MOI Household Registration 113年 (2024) township population density
key_finding: The positive NO2-income correlation (r=0.32) drops to near zero (partial r=0.05) after controlling for population density. Urbanization explains essentially all of the NO2-income association.
interpretation: NO2 concentration is strongly driven by population density (r=0.62), reflecting traffic and urban emission sources
Income is also positively correlated with density (r=0.45) in this station sample, since monitoring stations in Taiwan are disproportionately located in urban townships
After removing the shared density effect, income has essentially no independent association with NO2
PM2.5 shows no association with income either before or after density control
limitations: Population density is an imperfect proxy for urbanization; road density, traffic volume, and industrial activity are not directly measured
Only 78 of 368 townships have stations, and they are not a random sample of Taiwan townships
Station concentrations are not personal exposure
Three global missing dates not imputed
Numeric hours not certified valid hours
